newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to buy up to 200,000 T rice from Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Manila to buy up to 200,000 T rice from Malaysia.

text.p: The Philippine's state-owned National Food Authority has signed a contract to buy up to 200,000 tonnes of rice from Malaysia at $291.50 per tonne C&F, a senior Agriculture Department official told Reuters on Wednesday.
The official, who requested not to be identified, said the NFA has clinched a deal to buy 100,000 tonnes of rice from Malaysian International Trading Co.
"The contract also carried an option for NFA to buy an additional 100,000 tonnes of rice," the official said.
The contract with the Malaysian firm also stipulated that it can source "rice of the same grade" from neighbouring countries such as Thailand and Pakistan, the official said.
The Philippine Agriculture official said the rice order is for shipment between March and June this year.
The Malaysian rice order is part of the government's rice procurement programme to beef up supply of the country's staple before July when the harvest is low.

The NFA has so far signed agreements to buy 205,000 tonnes of rice from Thailand at $300 per tonne C&F. It has also signed separate contracts for the supply of 100,000 tonnes each from China and Vietnam at $291.50 per tonne C&F, with an option to buy an additional 100,000 tonnes each from both countries.
The NFA also allowed China to source rice from Thailand, Vietnam and Pakistan to meet its commitment.
